title: Developer Workbench: Sandbox Pricing, Onboarding, and Production Migration Brief
author: Harper Singh
body:
Overview

This brief describes the Developer Workbench (internal name: workbench-sandbox) — a hosted sandbox environment that lets engineers iterate with realistic inference traffic while controlling cost and telemetry. The goal is a low-friction path from experimentation to production-grade consumption: predictable pricing, reproducible telemetry, and a clear migration checklist to Dedicated/Private deployments.

Key objectives
- Give engineers a safe, budgeted sandbox that reflects production behavior (latency, KV/cache hits, token shapes).
- Provide transparent cost signals and an expected consumption-to-production delta.
- Automate migration artifacts (prompts, route configs, telemetry mappings) for handoff to platform teams.

Surface and capabilities
- Pre-configured runtime bundles: small, medium, and large sandbox SKUs with throughput backstops and token caps.
- Synthetic workload generator that can replay recorded developer sessions or simulate multi-tenant traffic shapes.
- Inline cost estimator in the console plus CLI: estimates token spend, expected throughput headroom, and warmup delta.
- Telemetry bridge: maps sandbox traces to production telemetry schemas (span names, token-level cost tags, KV cache hit ratios).
- Migration pack export: a zip that includes route definitions, prompt sets, telemetry mapping, and recommended quantization profile.

Pricing and packaging
- Monthly sandbox plan (free-trial + paid tiers):
  - Sandbox-S: $0/month baseline, 50K token cap/month, 10 concurrent sessions limit.
  - Sandbox-M: $199/month, 1M token cap, 50 concurrent sessions, priority queueing.
  - Sandbox-L: $999/month, 10M token cap, 250 concurrent sessions, warm capacity reservation (up to 10% of Dedicated burst pool).
- Overages billed at usage-rate multiplier (1.5x hosted API per-token rate) to keep sandbox cheap but discourage production workloads.
- Migration credit: on first Dedicated contract, up to 25% of paid sandbox months can be credited toward first Dedicated invoice (subject to customer eligibility).

Onboarding flow (developer-facing)
1) Sign up and select Sandbox tier.
2) Choose sample workload or upload recorded session.
3) Run preflight cost estimate and suggested runtime bundle.
4) Iterate on prompts and observe telemetry in the workbench console.
5) Export Migration pack when ready and open an onboarding request to Platform.

Migration checklist for platform handoff (owner: eng-platform)
1) Validate Migration pack artifacts and translate route configs into per-customer manifests.
2) Run synthetic traffic at 1x and 3x of observed sandbox peak to validate autoscaling policies.
3) Attach production SLA and billing contract; mark client allocation in capacity planner.
4) Configure telemetry lineage: ensure sandbox span -> production span mapping exists in tracing pipeline.
5) Execute blue-green rollout and monitor fidelity metrics for 72 hours.

Operational SLOs and guardrails
- Sandbox console availability: 99.9% monthly.
- Preflight estimator accuracy: predicted monthly token spend within ±15% for typical conversational workloads.
- Migration pack exports must succeed within 120s and include all required artifacts.
- Telemetry mapping completeness: >= 95% of sandbox spans must map to a production schema during onboarding checks.

Roadmap highlights (next 12 months)
- Q3 2026: Add configurable per-route fidelity presets and integration with Optimize suggestions.
- Q4 2026: Launch self-service Migration Pack validation checks with synthetic replay.
- Q1 2027: Add private workbench option for VPC-bound customers (onboarding for regulated verticals).

Release notes snapshot (initial GA 2026-04-06)
- Feature: Workbench GA with Sandbox-S/M/L and migration pack export.
- Telemetry: Initial bridge mapping to tracing and kv_hit_ratio metrics.
- Known limitations: Warm-capacity behavior in Sandbox-L is advisory; exact Dedicated warm reservations require formal contract.

Open decisions and risks
- Pricing delta between sandbox and hosted API: tradeoff between cheap experimentation and misuse for production. Proposal ties overages to 1.5x multiplier; monitor usage patterns for 90 days.
- Migration credit eligibility: requires minimum of 3 paid months or controlled pilot; may need exceptions for startups.
- Telemetry fidelity: current mapping covers conversational and request-level traces but lacks full per-token loss telemetry; prioritized for Q4 2026.

Appendix: CLI examples
- Estimate command:
  redwood workbench estimate --tier Sandbox-M --trace sample-session.json --out report.json
- Export migration pack:
  redwood workbench export-migration --project my-app --out my-app-migration.zip

If you are starting a pilot, open a request in the "Workbench Pilot" Jira component and tag the reviewers listed above.
